newsitem.title: GREECE: Ecu/drachma pierces 310 level, FRNs well bid.
newsitem.headline: Ecu/drachma pierces 310 level, FRNs well bid.

text.p: The drachma opened weaker against the ecu in early dealings on ecu buying from abroad with ecu/drachma piercing 310 resistance. Recently auctioned seven-year FRNs were well bid in the secondary market, dealers said.
Depos were little changed with overnight rates fluctuating in the 9.90-11.90 percent band and forex forwards were easier in longer tenors, traders said.

"Ecu/drachma opened at 309.90/95 but ecu buying from abroad has taken it higher to 310.12/18," said a forex dealer at a foreign bank. "I do not see a reason for this pick up but it might have to do with the Albanian elections."
Seven-year floaters auctioned on Thursday were well bid in the secondary market gaining some 20 to 30 basis points in terms of price.
Greece auctioned 150 billion drachmas of seven-year FRNs on Thursday. The first coupon was set at 10.40 percent. The gross selling commission was 1.10 percent.
The auction produced a cut-off price of 99.92 and an average price of 100.058.

"The outcome did not deviate from expectations with many accepted bids around par," said a foreign bank dealer. "Their prices have gained 20 to 30 basis points this morning and looks as if Greek banks got a good chunk."
The dealer said some banks were already in the market selling the FRNs to lock-in profits consisting mainly of the selling commission.
Depos were holding and long-term forex forwards were easier, money market dealers said.
"London banks must not have gotten a good portion out of the yesterday's auction and they have to somehow place their drachmas," said a dealer. "Offers in long forwards are easier."
The mark was quoted at 158.26/31 from Thursday's 158.110 fix, the dollar at 273.15/25 drachmas from 272.780 and the ecu at 310.32/42 from 309.940 drachmas.
